condition: Deep and organ-space surgical site infection in a diabetic patient (day 9)
permutationLabel: Organ-space SSI with sepsis, insulin-treated diabetes
summary: 67-year-old man with insulin-treated diabetes, day 9 after open right hemicolectomy: purulent wound, fever 38.9°C, HR 114, 6 cm subhepatic collection on CT, anastomosis intact; glucose 17.8.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Fever and pus from the wound after bowel operation
inputs.hpi: Day 9 after open right hemicolectomy (converted) for caecal cancer. Swinging fevers for 2 days, rigors last night, right upper abdominal pain, pus from the upper end of the midline wound. Eating a little, bowels open. Glucose readings in the high teens.

exam.general: Unwell. HR 114, BP 108/66, RR 22, SpO2 95% on air, T 38.9°C.
exam.abdomen: Upper midline wound: erythema 6 cm, purulent discharge, fascia intact. Tender right upper quadrant, no generalised peritonism.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast
imaging.result: 6 cm rim-enhancing subhepatic collection adjacent to the ileocolic anastomosis; no extraluminal contrast; subcutaneous wound collection.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Deep incisional and organ-space SSI (subhepatic collection) — day 9 after right hemicolectomy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Organ-space SSI with 6 cm subhepatic collection and deep wound infection, sepsis. Anastomosis intact on CT. IV antibiotics, CT-guided drainage, open wound, glycaemic control.

mustInclude.proposedFix: Add an organ/space SSI step to the SSI protocol: CT-guided percutaneous drainage of accessible collections (WSES 2017), relaparotomy for diffuse peritonitis.

guideline.name: NICE NG125 — Surgical site infections: prevention and treatment
guideline.section: 1.3 Antibiotic prophylaxis before clean surgery involving a prosthesis or implant, clean-contaminated and contaminated surgery; single dose IV on starting anaesthesia; do not use routinely for clean non-prosthetic uncomplicated surgery; take allergy and local resistance into account. 1.4 SSI treatment: antibiotic covering likely organisms, local resistance and culture results
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Surgical site infections: prevention and treatment (NG125). London: NICE; 2019 (updated 2020).

guideline.name: WSES guidelines — management of intra-abdominal infections
guideline.section: Early source control; CT for diagnosis; percutaneous drainage for accessible collections; relaparotomy for diffuse peritonitis; empirical antibiotics by severity and local resistance
guideline.citation: Sartelli M, Chichom-Mefire A, Labricciosa FM, et al. World J Emerg Surg. 2017;12:29.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign — international guidelines 2021
guideline.section: Antimicrobials within 1 h for possible septic shock or high likelihood of sepsis; source control as soon as practical; measure lactate; admit to ICU when needed
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063–143.

guideline.name: CPOC guideline — perioperative care for people with diabetes mellitus undergoing elective and emergency surgery
guideline.section: SGLT2 inhibitors: omit the day before and the day of surgery, check ketones; sulfonylureas omitted on the day of surgery; people with diabetes early on the list; capillary glucose monitoring; VRIII when more than one meal will be missed or in emergency surgery; type 1 diabetes: never omit basal insulin (continue long-acting insulin, usually at a reduced dose) alongside VRIII
guideline.citation: Centre for Perioperative Care. Guideline for perioperative care for people with diabetes mellitus undergoing elective and emergency surgery. London: CPOC; 2021 (updated 2022).

rationale: Permutation: deep/organ-space SSI with sepsis in a diabetic. Tests diagnosis, level, sepsis alarm, drainage, IV antibiotics and glycaemic control.
